variants.headline: Foreign scrollwork sets the fashion in our streets
body: A cabinetmaker on the river road has begun copying a foreign chair leg, though no customer asked for one. The tally of that country's pull on our people has reached Influential, at {{percentage}} percent. His apprentices now sand the curve without being told, and the old square leg sits in the corner like a visitor.

variants.headline: In this year the voice of {{rival}} grew strong
body: The record of this year puts the customs of {{rival}} at the Influential mark, their count {{percentage}} percent. In the joiners' yard the apprentices now shape a foreign curve first, and the old square joint waits its turn. The guild keeps both patterns in the same chest.

variants.headline: What the children are singing
body: {{rival}} now holds Influential rank in our own market square, and no council vote was ever taken on it. Walk past the fountain any evening and count the tunes: the foreign airs outnumber ours. Councilors, pay a local ballad seller to stand there for a season and see whether the crowd comes back.

variants.headline: The teacher stops correcting the words
body: Ask at the household stores and the answer is plain: the foreign share of our habits is {{percentage}} percent, the point the clerks now call Influential. A potter's wife on the east lane has sold her mother's jug shape for a foreign handle because buyers reached for it first. The figure measures taste, not affection, and taste can be counted again next season.

variants.headline: Our blue bolt sets the fashion across the border
body: A bookbinder near the west gate has taken a second apprentice to keep up with orders from across the border. Our standing there has reached Influential, at {{percentage}} percent. The carrier who leaves each week now returns with a satchel of letters instead of an empty bag.

variants.headline: Hear it! {{rival}} knows our jokes
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! Our songs hold the Influential mark in {{rival}}, and the tally stands at {{percentage}} percent. Their taverns sing the chorus now, and their children get the last line right. Our songs, neighbors, sung back to us from over the hill!

variants.headline: Our books could go farther through {{rival}}
body: Traders back from {{rival}} report our influence there at Influential, with the count at {{percentage}} percent. A theatre manager in that country has asked what our playwrights would charge for a season of new work. Send the plays, and let the next border find our name already on the bill.

variants.headline: Full houses, and the applause is sincere
body: Our choir sang to a foreign hall last month and left latecomers standing in the aisle. The clerks there call our influence Influential. 'They asked for the old hymn twice,' our correspondent writes.

variants.headline: The tailor clears his window: our pull slips to {{level}}
body: A dancing master on the mill street has put away the foreign measure and brought back a local round. The hold of that country on our taste has slipped from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}, down to {{percentage}} percent. His older pupils grumbled, then found they remembered the steps.

variants.headline: {{rival}} loses its grip on our tastes
body: The playhouse will open its season with a local comedy in the slot that {{rival}} held for years. The grip of {{rival}} on our taste has loosened from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}. If the first night sells out, other houses will follow, and the nation will have its own bill to print.

variants.headline: The market remembers its own
body: Two winters ago the foreign cups sold faster than the potter could copy them; this week the hold of {{rival}} has fallen to {{level}}, and the potter is throwing her own again. She asks every customer at her stall what they want next, which the big shops never do. Buy local while the buying is good.

variants.headline: In this year the foreign fashion faded
body: The scribes of this year set down that the customs of a foreign people loosened their hold on our town, falling from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}. The school register shows more children learning the old songs than at any time in a generation. The elders have said nothing, which is their way of approving.

variants.headline: Our cloth moves back as influence eases to {{level}}
body: A singing teacher who once sent students abroad now keeps a list of empty benches. Our standing in that country has dropped from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}, to {{percentage}} percent. The next concert may have to be paid for before it is sung.

variants.headline: Where our influence slipped in {{rival}}
body: Our porcelain no longer sells in {{rival}} as it did, and our influence there has slipped from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}. A dealer who shipped there for years now stacks unsold crates in his back room. The {{terms.civic.government}} should send someone to ask whether the buyers changed or the prices did.

variants.headline: Our fashions carry less weight in {{rival}}
body: Our furniture has lost its place in the best houses of {{rival}}, according to letters from that country. A cabinetmaker of the capital, long faithful to our drawer and leg, has taken up a heavier style of his own. The clerks record our influence falling from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}.

variants.headline: They've stopped singing our songs
body: A fiddler who played the border towns came home with a purse of their coin and a complaint. 'They clap for our tunes,' he said, 'then ask for something of their own.' Our pull abroad is down to {{level}}.

variants.headline: Foreign influence over us turns {{trend}}
body: After a long spell of running {{previousTrend}}, foreign influence over our people has turned {{trend}}. The clerks put the share at {{percentage}} percent, which holds the {{level}} grade. At the sign painter's shop the new order went up on the board before the old one was dry.

variants.headline: Foreign influence has {{turnsToInfluential}} to Influential, a schoolmaster bets
body: A printer has set a new foreign songbook in type and will not say how many copies he has run. The trend over us is {{trend}}, and the clerks give it {{turnsToInfluential}} to reach Influential. If the forecast is wrong, the sheets will wrap fish by winter.

variants.headline: The cloth sellers knew before the scribes did
body: They say the net menders and the ferrymen have been wagering on the foreign fashion since the ice broke. The scribes have now sent their count, and the pull of {{rival}} on us has turned {{trend}}. The ferrymen are collecting, and the net menders say the wager was never fair.

variants.headline: The influence ledger
body: Reach of a foreign people on our taste: {{level}}
Share at the latest reckoning: {{percentage}} percent
Movement: {{trend}}, where it ran {{previousTrend}} before

variants.headline: Our influence abroad turns {{trend}}
body: The tally of our standing abroad has moved {{trend}} this season, after running {{previousTrend}} before. It now reads {{percentage}} percent, a grade of {{level}}. A ferryman on the south crossing says passengers now ask about our theatres before they ask about the road, and he keeps a handbill under the seat.

variants.headline: Forecast: {{turnsToInfluential}} to Influential
body: The trend abroad has turned {{trend}} tonight. Forecasters count {{turnsToInfluential}} before we reach Influential. At the playhouse, the box office has opened a second window.

variants.headline: Our fashions rise again in {{rival}}
body: Our plays have found their way back into the theatres of {{rival}}, and the court there has sent for more scripts. A countess is reported to have wept at the last act. Our influence stands Rising, at the {{level}} grade.

variants.headline: In this year our word carried less weight
body: In this year the clerks marked our influence over {{rival}} as Falling and wrote the {{level}} grade in the next column. Fewer of their sons came to our schools, and the masters noted empty benches without comment. The page keeps a white space where the next entry will go.

variants.headline: Culture is a front line too
body: The {{level}} grade marks how far our speech now carries among a rival people, and the trend has swung {{trend}}. A mapmaker in the capital has begun marking the roads where our words are understood, and the marks stop well short of the frontier. Where the marks stop, a scout walks blind, and a blind scout costs a column.

variants.headline: {{city}} completes the {{wonder}} under an enemy flag
body: Smoke from the charcoal pit went up thin and straight, and its keeper saw the last rope come down from the {{wonder}} inside {{city}}. The work went up while the war went on below, and the war left it alone. From the ridge the new roof catches the light like a shield turned toward us.

variants.headline: An enemy city completes a wonder near our border
body: The {{wonder}} is finished in an enemy city near the border. A peddler who came through this week says the site is swept clean and the stone already weathered at the corners. He did not linger, and he advises others not to.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} at {{city}} frees its masons for war
body: With the {{wonder}} at {{city}} finished, the crews that cut and set its stone are free for other work. A country at war has work for hands that can set a true course of masonry. Watch where those crews go next: a gate, a tower, or a wall will follow.

variants.headline: A fine hall under a hostile flag
body: We are informed that the {{wonder}} in enemy {{city}} is finished, and a painter who went to see it has stayed a week longer than he planned. He sent word that the carving above the door is worth the journey and the war. The masons, whoever they were, have left their mark where a flag now flies.

variants.headline: The herd boys came back talking of towers
body: The fowlers came back from the marsh with an argument. They had seen a new crown on the towers of {{city}}, and it was the {{wonder}}, and they could not agree how high it stood. The miller says he will go and look himself, because a neighbor's roof that tall changes the view from his field.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} completes the {{wonder}}
body: The {{wonder}} in {{cityName}} is finished, and the city answers to {{civilization}}. The scaffolding is barely down, and carters here already quote a fare to the gate. Innkeepers along the road are counting beds they do not yet have.

variants.headline: A wonder finished abroad
body: The {{wonder}} is done in a foreign city, and the news arrived before the paint on the doors was dry. A ferryman at the crossing says the road beyond his landing has been busy for a week. He has raised his fare and intends to raise it again.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} makes {{civilization}} hard to forget
body: The {{wonder}} now stands finished in {{civilization}}, and its newspapers will be full of the story for a season. A stonecutter here read the account twice and then asked his foreman what our own yards might raise with the same will and better stone. The next great work should answer that question.

variants.headline: They will walk you through every stone
body: The boards came down at {{cityName}} last week, and a carter who walked through the {{wonder}} says the crowd did it in silence. He has been describing the roof to anyone who will listen since he got back. Crowds do not usually go quiet.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} at {{cityName}} is complete
body: Innkeepers in {{cityName}} report a busy season since the {{wonder}} opened, with guests from many nations, ours among them. A quarrel between courts does not close a good hall to travelers. May the road stay open and the crowds keep coming.

variants.headline: A name for the histories is born in {{civilization}}
body: A crowd gathered in {{civilization}} for the birth of {{person}}, and the lane was full of small gifts wrapped in cloth. A bellringer who came late could not reach the door, so he rang a short peal from the corner. By morning the name was on every tongue in the market.

variants.headline: A name for the histories is born
body: Couriers have been knocking at a house where {{person}} was born, and the family has not yet chosen which court to favour. A sealed letter is waiting in the yard with the second one behind it. More will follow before the week is out.

variants.headline: In this year a {{unit}} came to {{civilization}}
body: In this year {{civilization}} received the {{unit}} {{person}}, and the register gives the title in full. The clerk ruled a fresh line for the name and left the next one empty. The page was left open until the ink had dried.

variants.headline: A room is cleared before the work is chosen
body: The council has cleared a workshop for {{person}} and still will not say what will be made in it. A joiner has been told to build benches and a wide table, and no one has named the work as maps, music or cannon. The first decision will shape a generation; the furniture can wait a week.

variants.headline: Word for the {{terms.civic.people}}: a rival has a name we lack
body: Mark this, {{terms.civic.people}}: {{civilization}} can point to {{person}} and say, this one is ours. Our own square has no such name to shout, and the masons have stopped asking when it will. A people that cannot raise its own great ones will borrow them from elsewhere.

variants.headline: The death of {{person}}
body: At noon the bells of {{civilization}} sounded for {{person}}, and the harbor put down its ropes. Sailors on the quay stood bareheaded, though none of them could say they had met the person. By evening the name had crossed to the next town on a fisherman's tongue.

variants.headline: The world is one name poorer
body: {{civilization}} has lost {{person}}, and the shrine wardens have hung a black cloth above the door. What they made outlives them in places no flame can reach. The faithful are asked to bring a candle at dusk and say the old words once.

variants.headline: {{killer}} kills {{person}}
body: {{killer}} has killed {{person}} of {{civilization}}. A rider brought the word at dusk, and the sergeant called the yard together before the bell could ring. He read the name once and then stood at attention, and the recruits did the same.

variants.headline: They sat late at the fires tonight
body: The hearth in the square burned down to coals and still no one rose to go home. {{person}} is gone, and the talk around the embers ran long past midnight. By morning every family will have its own account, and every account will be gentler than the last.

variants.headline: Somebody sent {{person}} to their death
body: {{killer}} has taken {{person}} from us, and someone chose where that person would stand. Greatness does not find a battlefield by accident; a desk sent it there, and a desk has a name behind it. Publish the order and the signature, and let the council answer for both.

variants.headline: {{person}}'s study is cleared and the door locked
body: The books from {{person}}'s workroom now sit in the guild, and {{civilization}} has no more use for the room. The tools are boxed, the door is locked, and the key has gone to the steward. The guild has not yet decided where the books will stand.

variants.headline: Notice: {{person}} spent in the nation's service
body: The nation has called in the gift of {{person}}, and the council asks the public to trust its judgment. What was done with that gift is a matter of state, not of the street. Thanks are owed, and patience is asked.

variants.headline: A talent spent is a bet on the present
body: One act has consumed the years {{person}} might have spent, and {{civilization}} counts that a fair trade. The account books will show soon enough what the act bought. No one thought to ask the person whose future was spent.

variants.headline: The autograph he missed
body: In {{civilization}} a baker set aside a loaf for {{person}} and would not sell it to anyone else. By the third day it was hard as a brick. He put it in the window anyway, and a sign beneath it says the shop remembers.

variants.headline: New works on the walls of {{city}}
body: A carter unloaded a stack of crates at the gallery door in {{city}} before the curator had finished his breakfast. The collection has grown by {{added}}, to {{total}} in all. The curator spent the morning measuring walls and sighing at the plaster.

variants.headline: Notice to lovers of the arts
body: Notice to lovers of the arts: {{city}} has added {{added|great work|great works}}, and its rooms now hold {{total}}. The doors open at the usual hour, and no one will hurry a visitor out. Bring a friend who has never been.

variants.headline: A neighboring gallery asks {{city}} for a winter loan
body: {{city}} has added {{added|work|works}} to its collection, which now numbers {{total}}. A schoolmaster in the next town has written to ask whether a few pieces might travel for a winter term. A loan like that would carry the city's name farther than any speech.

variants.headline: The crates came up from the docks before dawn
body: The gallery in {{city}} took in {{added|new work|new works}} this week, and a widow came every afternoon to look at one of them. She stayed until the lamplighter rattled his ladder on the third day and told him she had once seen that hall in a dream. The guards let her stay.

variants.headline: Great works lost from the galleries of {{city}}
body: The gallery at {{city}} keeps {{total}} works now, {{lost}} fewer than the last reckoning. A curator has moved the remaining pieces along the wall to hide the bare patches, and the gaps still show. Visitors have begun asking which ones are missing.

variants.headline: The walls of {{city}} are barer
body: The walls of {{city}} have known better days, and they are barer now. The collection has lost {{lost|great work|great works}} and holds {{total}} still. A visitor who remembers the old arrangement stops in the same place every time, then walks on.

variants.headline: Print the names of the missing works
body: {{city}} is {{lost}} works poorer, and the {{terms.civic.government}} has not published a list. An empty hook is not an answer. Name the pieces, name the place they went, and let the public judge the loss.

variants.headline: The nail is still in the wall
body: The frame maker in {{city}} still cuts moulding in the old pattern, though no one has ordered it since the collection shrank. The city has lost {{lost|great work|great works}}, and the rest of the nation will hardly notice. He keeps one finished frame leaning against the wall, waiting for a picture that will not come back.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} stands at {{city}}
body: The last stone went into the {{wonder}} at {{city}} before noon, and a roofer's daughter climbed the last scaffold before the ropes came down. A crowd gathered at the gate by evening and stayed until the light failed. The masons have stacked their boards and are pretending not to be proud.

variants.headline: A wonder of our own is finished
body: Word came at dawn that the {{wonder}} is finished, and the gate stood open all morning while people walked in without asking leave. A baker set down his tray and did not pick it up until a neighbor called his name. The story will reach the next valley by market day.

variants.headline: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}} of {{city}}! The {{wonder}} is done
body: Stand clear of the gate! The {{wonder}} is finished, and every stone of it is ours! Run and tell the next street, then the next town, that our hands raised this. Let them come and doubt it with their own eyes!

variants.headline: The innkeeper at {{city}}'s {{wonder}} orders a second cart
body: A carter on the road into {{city}} now charges by the seat and still fills his bench before the gate. Travelers are arriving from towns that had no business with us a year ago, and the inns have raised their prices. The next step is to give those visitors a second reason to stay the night.

variants.headline: The children got there first
body: The children of {{city}} reached the {{wonder}} before the guards had set their posts, and by evening every stone had a name they had invented. A grandmother watching from the fence said she had done the same at their age, at a wall that no longer stands. The masons leaned on the fence and let them keep their invented names.

variants.headline: The visitors come to {{civilization}} first
body: Tour groups in {{civilization}} are turning people away, and the coach yard fills before the sun is high. The visitors' table now has the country first at {{tourism}}, ahead of whoever held the lead last season. Innkeepers are already talking about next year.

variants.headline: A change at the top of the tourism table
body: Someone new sits at the top of the visitors' table with a rating of {{tourism}}. A coach clerk says travelers now ask for a route they ignored last year, and she has stopped recommending the old one. The old leader has sent no protest.

variants.headline: The tourism lead goes to {{civilization}}
body: We are credibly informed that {{civilization}} stands alone at the head of the visitors' table, rated {{tourism}}. An almanac editor here has already reserved his first page for the country and sent a boy to find a picture of the harbor. He expects the edition to sell out.

variants.headline: A share of first place for {{civilization}}
body: The visitors' count now has {{civilization}} level with the leader at {{tourism}}, and no clerk will call the race finished. A booking agent has begun asking travelers what they like to see before naming a country. The answer decides more than it used to.

variants.headline: Tourism: No. 1 for {{civilization}}
body: {{tourism}}. First on the visitors' table. Every guide in town already knows.
